title: Frameworks, CI, fuzz, benchmarks, packaging and collateral
obligations: Read test/e2e/benchmark framework wiring, assertion oracles, fixture isolation, scenario selection/skip behavior, process control, resource gates and compiler-free restore checks; a green run does not prove integrity.

Review CI, mutation diff scopes, workflow policy/authorization, fuzz target/corpus, benchmark gate statistics, release signing/version consistency and package install/uninstall paths for meaningful guardrails.
Account explicitly for benchmark-only subjects, generated lockfiles, binary fixtures, demo/media assets and licenses; distinguish fully read configuration/frameworks from sampled workload executions.
Restrict primary statements to this exact sub-scope path list; inspect declared neighboring seams as consultation, with no double primary ownership.

contracts.quote: `just check` is not the merge gate. CI mutation-tests changed Rust lines in the kache binary. A PR that only ran `cargo test` on the new tests will go red on Mutation testing. That is the usual failure.

owned_interactions.contract: Cargo metadata/build.rs/install assets/scripts/Helm/Nix ↔ service/config/shim behavior; installed artifacts and version contracts
kache-e2e/scripts/CI/scenario oracles ↔ each domain-specific test; real compiler/process/remote observations and meaningful failure discrimination

consult_interactions.contract: kache-e2e/scripts/CI/scenario oracles ↔ each domain-specific test; real compiler/process/remote observations and meaningful failure discrimination

sampling_needs: Read harness/CI/package configurations fully; executing all 70+ scenario subjects and cloud/package ecosystems is outside one local review and must be declared sampled.
Binary/media collateral receives identity/purpose/reference accounting, not semantic code-review claims; exported benchmarks are workload-specific.
Read every assigned production path in full. Large dedicated test suites may be sampled only with named ranges/cases and exact omissions in the report.
expected_coverage_report: Record every path as fully read, sampled with bounds, or pending. Mapped is not reviewed. Fully read production/framework/configuration paths and explicitly record runtime sampling.
